Morning is probably the best approach for average people. You don't need a lot of weight, and you probably won't hurt yourself. For the type of lifting I do, I'll have more energy in the afternoon or evening, and I won't be groggy or uncoordinated. I also tend to be a night rat in general, but if you have a normal job and schedule you probably don't want to be up late, and working out before bed has never made me want to go to sleep.

There is always going to be someone doing it differently and claiming it is best for them. That said, here are things I have observed.

Running I find easiest to get out of the way in the morning, right when I get up. You are better served by having eaten something as there is no solid science behind the idea of "fasted running" on an empty, early morning tank, and any extra fat calories burned would be pretty much minimal. That said, I run before I eat, as I said, when I first get up. Unless you are running for well over 90 minutes you shouldn't need any fuel for your run. On long runs, take some fuel and water, of course.

Weights I find best in the afternoon. I do recall seeing some data supporting this, so you could probably find some with some searching. Basically, you are fueled up from breakfast and lunch, and probably most alert and are not feeling depleted that early in the day, thus solid results.
